result: {"findings": [{"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 320, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "getResult drops the drained check, so a closed queue cannot tell a spurious wake from a real drain", "body": "The old code asserted `node == null and self.closed and self.pending.isEmpty()` before returning `error.Closed`. The new code returns `error.Closed` from an empty queue without reading `closed` or `pending` at all, while `wait` (line 185) and `timedWait` (line 218) still make that check. The escape hatch the new comment offers works for one caller only: \"the caller that knows it never closed the queue\". A caller that DID close the queue is the documented shutdown shape (module doc lines 38-49, and `cancelAll(.keep)` at lines 17-20), and it cannot apply the workaround. Failure: the driver calls `close()`, an operation is still in flight, a stale wake wins the select arm, `getResult` returns `error.Closed`, the driver reads that as \"closed and fully drained\" (the contract at line 174), stops draining and frees the queue. The heap-backed operations that were still in `pending` are never handed out, so their memory leaks and their completions land on a dead queue. The pop is already under the mutex; keeping the `closed and pending.isEmpty()` read there costs nothing and lets the function return `error.Closed` only when it is true."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 86, "severity": "major", "category": "docs", "title": "Three contract statements in this file still promise the strict reading of a wake that getResult abandoned", "body": "The change updated only the comment inside `getResult`. Three other statements in the same file now say the opposite of what the code does. Line 85-86: \"The future protocol depends on the strict reading of a wake: a completion is takeable, or the queue is drained.\" Line 280-281: \"The registered wait completes when a completion is ready to be taken or the queue is drained; getResult then pops one like next, or reports error.Closed.\" Lines 55-57: \"The winning result is what `wait` would have returned\", which is false because `wait` never returns `error.Closed` on an open, non-empty queue and `getResult` now can. A reader who starts from the type documentation, which is where a consumer starts, gets the old guarantee and writes the teardown that finding one describes. Fix the three statements to say that a select arm may report `error.Closed` spuriously, and say what the caller must do."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 302, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The new spurious error.Closed path has no test and no diagnostic", "body": "The assertion was the only thing that reported the upstream protocol bug. It is now replaced by a return value that is byte-identical to the normal drained result, so the bug is silent: no counter, no debug-mode log, no test. The file's other contract changes each carry a named regression test (#673, #677). Here nothing exercises the new path, so a future edit that makes a genuine drain return the wrong value, or that makes the stale wake common, produces the same output as a healthy run and no test fails. At minimum, add a test that drives `getResult` on an open empty queue through the future protocol and pins the documented outcome, and keep a runtime-safety-only counter or `std.log.debug` on the branch so the upstream bug stays observable."}]}
